thesis: Margin compression is cost-driven and reversible (bull) vs structural private-label pressure (bear)

supporting_evidence.quote: The margin compression is input costs and packaging, not demand, and the new CEO's cost program will reverse it
a new CEO cost program with a stated target of restoring gross margin above 24% within eight quarters

counterevidence.quote: net sales decreased 4.2% and gross margin compressed to 21.3% from 24.8% a year ago
Private label share gains in packaged foods are structural and a cost program does not fix a pricing problem

primary.quote: Net sales decreased 4.2% compared with the prior-year quarter
Gross margin was 21.3% compared with 24.8% in the prior-year quarter

verification.note: needs a price; the 10-Q gives only the $0.31 quarterly dividend

unresolved_questions: How much of the 4.2% sales decline is volume versus price, by segment?
Is the dividend covered by free cash flow after the cost program's restructuring charges?
